decisions.rationale: With limited budget, test maximally distant settings from the baseline (s1=A, s2=A, s3=A) to assess main effects across all three dimensions simultaneously.
Config 2 achieved much lower f1 with s1=A, while Config 1 had lower f2 with s2=B. Testing s1=A with s2=B and s3=A may reduce f2 without sacrificing f1.
s2=A strongly reduced f1 compared to s2=B under s1=A. Testing s1=A, s2=A with s3=D evaluates whether s3=D restores the lower f2 observed in configuration 1.
Evaluating s1=E with s2=A and s3=D leverages the strong performance of s2=A observed previously, potentially reducing both costs compared to config 1 to push the Pareto frontier further.
Explore the effect of setting s1=A, which also deactivates s2, holding s3 at baseline to isolate s1's contribution.
s1=A dramatically lowered f1 with minimal impact on f2. Exploring variations in s3 under s1=A to investigate if f2 can be improved further.
s1=A strongly improved f1 at a small cost to f2. Testing s1=B explores whether another s1 label achieves low f1 while matching or beating D's low f2.
Explore untested s1=C and s2=A with baseline s3=B, aiming to discover configurations that achieve lower f1 than D while reducing f2 below A's level.
Explore a distant point across all sites to establish diverse baselines and identify potential improvements over the default configuration.
Evaluating s1=A with baseline s2=B and s3=D to test if s1=A alone drives the massive f1 reduction while retaining baseline's low f2.
s1=D achieved the lowest f2 while s2=A, s3=A yielded the lowest f1. Testing their combination s1=D, s2=A, s3=A may yield an ideal trade-off or potentially dominate existing points.
Effects appear additive with s2=A, s3=A sharply minimizing f1. Testing untested s1=B with the best (s2=A, s3=A) settings could yield lower costs on either objective.
Baseline evaluated. Test diverse values across all sites by switching s1 to A, s2 to A, and s3 to A to discover contrasting cost trade-offs.
Config 2 achieved very low f1 with s1=A, while config 1 achieved lower f2 with s2=B and s3=B. Combining s1=A with s2=B, s3=B tests potential Pareto improvement.
Testing s1=A, s2=A with s3=B isolates s2 vs s3, potentially combining the low f1 seen with s2=A/s3=A and the low f2 seen with s3=B.
s2=A drastically reduced f1 without hurting f2 on s1=A. Testing s1=D with s2=A and s3=B may retain the optimal f2 (3200) while substantially lowering f1.
Explore orthogonal variations by testing s1=A and s2=A with a different s3 label to observe main effects away from the baseline.
Test s1=A with the original s2=B and s3=A settings to isolate whether s1=A maintains its low f1 while restoring low f2.
Evaluating s1=A, s2=A, s3=A isolates the effect of s2=A versus s3=B from previous evaluations, potentially achieving low f1 while improving f2 over configuration 2.
Switching s2 to A drastically reduced f1 without worsening f2 in s1=A. Testing s1=D with s2=A and s3=A aims to achieve f2=3200 with significantly improved f1.
Explore a distant configuration across all three sites to establish diverse baseline points across the search space.
Isolate the impact of s1=A versus original settings s2=B and s3=D, seeking to combine the lower f1 of configuration 2 with the lower f2 of configuration 1.
Testing s1=A with s2=B and s3=A isolates the impact of s3=A on f1 while attempting to retain the lower f2 from s2=B.
s2=A drastically reduced f1 while s3=D significantly reduced f2 in evaluated s1=A configurations. Combining s2=A with s3=D may yield an optimal trade-off.
s2=A drastically reduced f1 compared to s2=B across previous tests. Testing s1=E with s2=A and s3=D may retain the lowest observed f2 (3200) while substantially lowering f1.
s2=A and s3=D consistently produce the lowest costs. Testing s1=B with s2=A, s3=D explores whether s1=B offers a superior intermediate or dominant trade-off between f1 and f2.
Testing s1=D with the high-performing s2=A and s3=D combination to explore whether s1=D yields an even better Pareto trade-off between f1 and f2.
s1=C is the only unexplored branch of s1, where s2 is bypassed. Testing s1=C with s3=D (the best known s3 value) checks for potentially dominant trade-offs.
s2=A consistently outperforms s2=B. Testing unexplored site s3=B with s1=E and s2=A targets the lowest f2 region to potentially improve upon the current minimum f2 of 3136.
Explore a structurally distinct configuration, testing s1=A (where s2 is inactive) and s3=A to establish baseline sensitivity relative to the original.
Isolate the effect of s1=A versus s1=D by evaluating s1=A with s3=B, directly comparing with the baseline to see if low f1 persists while recovering low f2.
s1=A drastically reduces f1 while slightly increasing f2. Test unexplored branch s1=B with s2=A and s3=B to probe whether another main branch lowers both costs or improves f2.
Testing s1=B with s2=B to check if s2=B significantly reduces f2 compared to s2=A while retaining the low f1 seen in evaluation 4.
Switching s2 from B to A substantially reduced f1 on s1=B. Testing s2=A with s1=D could achieve a superior trade-off by combining low f1 with s1=D's low f2 baseline.
s2=A consistently yields large f1 reductions. Testing unobserved s1=C with s2=A and s3=B to probe for better trade-offs along the Pareto frontier.
Testing unexplored s1=E with the high-performing s2=A and s3=B combination to explore potential improvements on both objectives.
Configurations with s2=A consistently dominate s2=B. Since s1=D achieved the best f2 (3136), testing unexplored values of s3 (such as C) under s1=D, s2=A may further optimize f1 and f2.
s1=D and s2=A yielded the lowest f2 so far (3136). Testing unexplored label s3=D in this configuration may push f2 even lower along the Pareto frontier.
Varying s1 to label A while keeping other sites at baseline values to test sensitivity along s1.
Screening another s1 label while holding s2 and s3 at baseline to isolate the main effect of s1 across the trade-off.
Screening remaining s1 values while holding s2 and s3 constant. s1=B yielded low f1 with modest f2 cost; s1=C may improve the trade-off further.
Evaluating the remaining unmeasured label s1=E with baseline s2 and s3 to understand its main effect across both objectives.
s1=E achieves dramatically lower f1 while keeping f2 modest. With s2 ignored when s1=E, we now vary s3 to see if f2 can be reduced further.
s1=E yields the lowest f1, while s1=D has the lowest f2. Label s2=A has not been explored yet; testing it on s1=D checks for improvements on f2.
Switching s2 to A significantly reduced both f1 and f2 for s1=D. Testing s1=C with s2=A may combine low f1 and favorable f2, potentially yielding a new non-dominated point.
Switching s2 to A significantly dropped f1 across configurations. Since s1=B had lower f1 than s1=C with s2=B, s1=B with s2=A may establish a new best minimum for f1.
Switching s2 to A consistently reduces f1 by ~40,000 across all s1 labels; evaluating s1=A with s2=A is projected to achieve the global minimum f1.
Explore the effect of mutating site s1 to A while holding other parameters at baseline to determine main effects on f1 and f2.
s1=A significantly lowered f1 compared to D. Testing s2=A holding s1=A and s3=B assesses s2's impact on both objectives.
s2=A yielded a huge f1 reduction on s1=A without impacting f2. Testing s1=D with s2=A may retain the lowest f2 (3200) while drastically improving f1.
s2=A consistently and substantially reduces f1. We keep s2=A and s3=B fixed while exploring untested s1=C to test whether s1 contains labels that further improve the Pareto front.
s2=A consistently and substantially reduces f1. Since s3 has only been evaluated at B, varying s3 with the low-f2 base (s1=D, s2=A) tests for potential joint improvements.
s2=A consistently slashes f1 while maintaining low f2. Exploring unexplored label s1=E with s2=A, s3=B tests whether s1=E can dominate or improve trade-offs against s1=A and s1=D.
s1 labels {C, E, A, D} form a smooth Pareto trade-off with s2=A, s3=B. Testing s1=B (which ignores s2) explores the remaining unseen label for s1 to check if it extends the frontier.
s1=D and s2=A yield the lowest f2 so far. Testing untested label s3=C on this base could discover a new minimum for f2 or improve the trade-off.
s3 strongly controls f2 while s1=D, s2=A achieves the lowest f2 so far. Testing untested s3=D explores whether f2 can be reduced further along the Pareto frontier.
Explore distinct label assignments across all sites to establish baselines and identify favorable regions away from the original configuration.
Test s1=A with original settings s2=B, s3=A to see if the large f1 reduction from s1=A can combine with the lower f2 of s2=B, s3=A.
Isolating s2=A with s1=A, s3=A to check whether s2=A drives the low f1 in evaluation 2 while maintaining low f2 from s3=A.
s2=A drastically reduced f1 compared to s2=B with no f2 penalty. Testing unexplored s1=B with the promising s2=A and s3=A settings to search for improvements across both objectives.
s1=D achieved the best f2 (3200), and switching s2 from B to A drastically reduced f1 under s1=A without harming f2. Testing s1=D, s2=A, s3=A could yield a superior trade-off.
s2=A and s3=A consistently optimize both costs across known s1 variants. Evaluating unexplored s1=E with s2=A, s3=A may discover better trade-offs or extend the Pareto front.
Testing the unexplored s1=C branch with s3=A to determine its baseline effect across both objectives, where s2 is inactive.
s2=A strongly outperforms B. Exploring unexplored site s3=C with the high-performing s1=B, s2=A base could further reduce f1 or f2 along the promising low-f1 frontier.
Combining s1=D and s2=A (which yields the lowest f2) with s3=C (which demonstrated lower f1 than s3=A in run 9) targets a potential Pareto improvement over configuration 6.
Test label A on site s1 while holding s2 and s3 at baseline to isolate s1's main effect across the objective space.
Isolate the effect of site s2 by testing s2=A while holding s1=A and s3=D constant relative to the best f1 configuration.
Holding the best f1 settings s1=A and s2=A constant, evaluate s3=A to test the impact of s3 on both objectives.
s2=A dramatically reduced f1 without worsening f2 in s1=A. Testing s1=E with s2=A and s3=D could significantly reduce f1 while maintaining low f2=3200.
s2=A consistently outperforms s2=B across evaluated s1 settings. Testing unexplored label s1=B with s2=A and s3=D to discover potentially superior trade-offs between f1 and f2.
s2=A with s3=D consistently yields strong Pareto points across s1=E, A, B. Evaluating s1=D explores whether it further minimizes f1 or f2 before testing other s3 labels.
Evaluating untested branch s1=C with the best known s3=D to test whether s1=C offers superior f1 or f2 trade-offs while ignoring s2.
s1=E and s2=A achieved the best f2 cost so far. Testing untested label s3=B on this base configuration to explore if f2 can be reduced further.
Testing unexplored label C for s3 on the top f2-performing base s1=E, s2=A to explore potential reductions in f2 or improvements along the trade-off.
s3=C significantly reduced both f1 and f2 on s1=E. Testing s3=C with s1=B and s2=A may combine the lowest f1 branch with optimal f2 performance.
s3=C yielded major improvements for s1=E and s1=B. Since s1=A previously had lower f2 than s1=B with s3=D, combining s1=A, s2=A, and s3=C should yield a strong Pareto trade-off.
Label s3=C yielded major improvements for both objectives. Testing untested label s3=E with top-performing s1=A and s2=A checks if s3=E offers further Pareto gains or dominates s3=C.
s3=C and s2=A yield the best trade-offs. Testing s1=D with s2=A, s3=C to check if s1=D's lower f1 seen with s3=D produces an extreme minimum for f1 on the Pareto front.
s3=C dramatically reduces both objectives across all tested s1 values. Testing unexplored s1=C with s3=C could yield a new non-dominated trade-off.
Vary s2 to A while keeping s1 and s3 fixed at baseline values to isolate the effect of s2 on both objectives.
s2=A substantially improved both f1 and f2. Holding s1=D and s2=A fixed, explore s3=A to observe the influence of s3 on the objectives.
s2=A substantially reduces f1 compared to s2=B, with s3=B yielding lower costs than s3=A. We explore new values of s1, keeping s2=A and s3=B to seek further reductions.
s2=A and s3=B perform well. Exploring s1=C with s2=A and s3=B to probe a new region of the trade-off between f1 and f2.
s2=A and s3=B consistently perform best across tested configurations. Evaluating unexplored s1=E alongside s2=A and s3=B to search for lower costs along the trade-off.
s1=A remains untested across all evaluated configurations. Evaluating s1=A with s3=B will reveal whether it achieves a superior trade-off against the existing Pareto front.
s1=C, s2=A provides low f1 with moderate f2. We test s3=C to explore whether other labels for s3 can reduce f2 without sacrificing f1.
s1=E with s2=A achieved a strong balance of low f1 and f2; testing unexplored label s3=D to probe for lower f2.
Config 9 with s3=D showed a dramatic reduction in both objectives on s1=E and s2=A. Evaluating s3=E tests whether the remaining s3 label achieves even lower costs on the best known baseline.
s3=D delivered a major reduction in both f1 and f2. Combining s3=D with s1=C, which showed lower f1 than s1=E at s3=B, tests for potential global improvements.
s3=D drastically reduces both costs. Evaluating s1=B with s2=A and s3=D tests whether s1=B's lower baseline f1 achieves a new minimum for f1 on the Pareto front.
Evaluating s1=D, s2=A, s3=D tests if s1=D's uniquely low baseline f2 translates via s3=D's consistent -768 f2 delta into a new non-dominated trade-off with the lowest overall f2.
Evaluating the promising s3=D slice on the remaining unexplored choice s1=A to test for potential Pareto improvements in f1 and f2.
Testing s2=B with the promising s1=E and s3=D combination to check whether s2 provides an unexplored trade-off or further reduces f2.
Baseline established at (D, B, D). Test alternative label A on s1 while holding s2 and s3 constant to measure s1's marginal impact on both objectives.
Baseline s1=A reduced f1 considerably. Test s2=A alongside s1=A and s3=D to isolate the impact of s2 on both objectives.
s1=A and s2=A gave an excellent reduction in f1. Testing s3=A evaluates the effect of s3 variation on this promising subspace.
Changing s2 to A significantly reduced f1 for s1=A. Testing s1=D with s2=A and s3=A may drastically reduce f1 while maintaining s1=D's low f2.
s2=A significantly reduces f1 while maintaining low f2 for s1=D. Testing unexplored s1=B with s2=A, s3=A checks for further improvements on both objectives.
s1=B offered strong f1 with much lower f2 than s1=A. Testing s1=C with the best settings s2=A and s3=A checks if s1=C achieves lower f2 or dominates current points.
Testing unexplored s1=E with s3=A to discover where s1=E lies on the f1-f2 trade-off spectrum relative to labels A through D.
s2=A consistently yields low f1. Having explored all s1 options with s3=A, we now explore untried labels for s3, testing whether s3=B can improve upon the strong trade-off at s1=B, s2=A.
Run 9 revealed that s3=B significantly lowered both objectives with s1=B, s2=A. Testing s3=C with this promising base evaluates whether other s3 labels yield further improvements.
Configuration s1=B, s2=A yielded a dominant result with s3=B. Testing remaining unexplored label s3=E on this strong baseline to check for further improvements or trade-offs.
Label s3=B dramatically reduced both costs for s1=B, s2=A. Since s1=C had lower f2 than s1=B when s3=A, evaluating s1=C, s2=A, s3=B could yield an even lower f2.
Label s3=B consistently reduces f1 and f2 by fixed offsets. Since s1=D achieved the lowest f2 on s3=A, evaluating s1=D with s2=A and s3=B should discover a new Pareto minimum for f2.
s1=A achieves the lowest baseline f1 across all tested values, and s3=B strongly reduces both f1 and f2. Testing s1=A, s2=A, s3=B could yield a new minimum for f1.
s3=B provides the lowest costs across both objectives. Testing s1=E with s3=B completes the evaluation of s1 variants on s3=B to probe for new Pareto optimal points.
Varying s1 to label A while keeping s2 and s3 at original values helps isolate the main effect of s1 on both objectives.
Explore label C for s1 while holding s2 and s3 at baseline to map the main effect of s1 on both objectives.
Screening remaining s1 label E while holding s2 and s3 constant to identify whether it yields further f1 reductions without the f2 penalty observed in C.
Complete the one-factor sweep of s1 by evaluating s1=B (which ignores s2) against the baseline s3=B to identify if it yields further Pareto improvements.
s1=B substantially cuts f1. Since s2 is ignored when s1=B, we fix s1=B and explore s3 variation starting with s3=A to discover trade-offs or further cost reductions.
s1=B dramatically lowers f1. Testing unvisited s3 values with s1=B (where s2 is ignored) may uncover lower f2 values to dominate existing Pareto points.
s1=B provides the lowest f1 by far; evaluate untested label s3=D to search for lower f2 values under this promising branch.
Evaluating the final unexplored s3 label with s1=B to check if s3=E can further reduce f2 and establish full dominance.
All s1=B variants are explored. Since s3=E dramatically reduced both objectives and s1=D previously achieved the lowest f2 among baseline runs, pairing s1=D with s3=E may yield an even lower f2.
s3=E significantly lowered both objectives. Site s2 has not been tested with label A yet; evaluating s1=A, s2=A, s3=E checks whether s2=A further improves costs or trades off against s1=B.
s2=A significantly reduced f1 with s3=E in run 11. Testing s1=E with s2=A and s3=E could improve upon s1=A, exploring a potential Pareto-dominating configuration.
s2=A and s3=E yield the lowest costs; testing s1=C with s2=A and s3=E should achieve the lowest f1 based on s1 baseline rankings.
Label s2=A dramatically reduced f1 across A, E, and C with s3=E. Since s1=D with s3=E had a best-in-class f2 of 2496, testing s1=D with s2=A may yield a Pareto improvement.
Test whether s1=E with s2=B and s3=E achieves a lower f2 than s2=A, potentially improving the objective near the optimal region.
Isolate the main effect of site s1 by evaluating s1=A while holding s2=B and s3=A constant relative to the baseline configuration.
Testing s2=A with s1=A and s3=A to isolate the impact of site s2 on the trade-off.
Switching s2 from B to A drastically reduced f1 without hurting f2. Testing s1=D with s2=A may retain the lower f2 of 3200 while decreasing f1.
s2=A consistently yields major f1 reductions. Evaluate s1=B with s2=A and s3=A to probe another s1 label along the promising s2=A baseline.
Screening remaining s1 labels with the high-performing s2=A and s3=A baseline to check if s1=E further optimizes f1 or f2.
Evaluate the last untested label for s1 (C), which also ignores s2, to complete the main-effect exploration of s1 on the baseline s3=A.
Varying unexplored site s3 while fixing the best trade-off anchor s1=D, s2=A to explore potential improvements across both objectives.
s1=D, s2=A gives the lowest f2 so far. We test s3=C to explore whether other s3 labels improve f2 or f1 over the baseline s3=A.
s2=A is strictly superior. Exploring s3 variants on the best f2 base (s1=D, s2=A) tests if s3=D yields an even lower f2 than s3=A.
Testing s3=E with optimal s1=D, s2=A to explore if it achieves an even lower f2 than s3=A.
s3=E significantly reduced both f1 and f2 in run 11. Testing s3=E with s1=B and s2=A combines the lowest f1 configuration with the best s3 setting to discover new Pareto points.
Label s3=E yielded dramatic improvements in both objectives. Testing s1=A with s2=A and s3=E may produce a superior trade-off point between D's low f2 and B's low f1.
s1=E achieved the lowest f1 with s3=A. Testing s1=E with s2=A and the high-performing s3=E may establish a new minimum for f1 on the Pareto front.
Testing s1=C with the optimal s3=E setting completes evaluating all s1 choices on the promising trade-off frontier.
Explore an opposite extreme of the search space with new labels across all sites to quickly detect main effects and establish baselines.
Isolate s2's effect when s1=A and s3=A to see if s2=B improves f2 while maintaining the low f1 achieved in turn 2.
s2=A yielded much better f1 and slightly lower f2 than s2=B. Testing s1=A with s2=A and s3=D to combine low f1 with the lower f2 observed with s3=D.
s2=A strongly improves f1 over s2=B, and s3=D improved f2 over s3=A. We evaluate s3=B with s1=A, s2=A to explore whether other s3 labels further reduce f2.
Evaluating s3=C with the best performing base s1=A and s2=A to check if another s3 label further reduces f2 below 3328.
s1=A and s2=A consistently yield low costs, with s3 strongly driving f1 and f2 reductions. Testing s3=E explores the remaining unseen label for s3 in this promising sub-space.
Fixing the best observed values s2=A and s3=C while exploring s1=B to check if alternative labels at s1 improve upon the Pareto-optimal configuration #6.
s3=C produces the lowest costs so far. Having tested s1=A and s1=B with s2=A and s3=C, we test unexplored s1=D with the winning combination (s2=A, s3=C).
s3=C produces the best trade-offs; testing s1=C (which ignores s2) with s3=C explores the remaining unseen label for s1 on the promising frontier.
s3=C consistently minimizes both costs, while s2=A drastically reduces f1 over s2=B. s1=E yielded lower f2 than s1=A on s3=D, so testing s1=E with s2=A and s3=C could improve the Pareto front.
Testing s1=D with s3=D to check whether s1=D has an alternate optimal s3 label that lowers its high f2 (4160) while maintaining low f1.
All s1 variants with s2=A and s3=C are evaluated and form the Pareto front. Testing s1=B with s2=B and s3=C checks if s2=B offers an unexplored trade-off or lower f2 on non-A sites.
All s1 values evaluated with s3=C form the current front. Testing s1=C with s3=B checks if non-C labels for s3 can further reduce f2 below 2496 while maintaining competitive performance.
Test s1=D with s2=A and s3=B to probe whether alternative s3 values on the lowest-f1 site yield an unexpected interaction or improved trade-off.
Test s1=D with s2=B and s3=C to investigate whether s2=B reduces f2 on the s1=D Pareto-optimal branch.
With all s3=C configurations tested, testing s1=C with s3=D checks if s3=D can yield a lower f1 or f2 under the lowest-f2 branch s1=C.
With s3=C dominating f1, we explore s1=C with s3=E to verify whether an alternative s3 label under s1=C can achieve a new minimum for f2 below 2496.
Evaluating s1=C with s3=A completes the s1=C sweep, verifying whether s3=A exhibits any unexpected low cost trade-offs under s1=C.
Testing s1=B with s2=A and s3=D to explore if s1=B yields improved trade-offs outside the prominent s3=C subspace.
Vary s2 to A while keeping s1 and s3 fixed to isolate the main effect of s2 against the baseline.
s2=A showed substantial improvements across both objectives over s2=B. Testing s3=A with s1=D and s2=A to explore s3's influence on the objective values.
s2=A substantially improved f1 and f2 over s2=B, with s3=B performing well. Testing s1=B with the promising settings s2=A and s3=B explores the impact of site s1.
Evaluating s1=C with the best known settings s2=A and s3=B to explore s1's trade-off space between f1 and f2.
Explore untested s1=E with high-performing settings s2=A and s3=B to probe for lower costs along the Pareto front.
Evaluating the remaining unvisited label for s1 (s1=A, where s2 is ignored) with the favorable s3=B to explore potential gains in f1 or f2.
s1=E with s2=A achieved near-optimal f1 with the lowest f2 among low-f1 configurations. Testing unexplored label s3=C on this base to check if f2 can be reduced further.
Testing unexplored label s3=D with strong candidates s1=C and s2=A to check if it improves f2 while keeping f1 competitive.
s3=D with s1=C yielded major improvements on both objectives. Evaluating s3=E with s1=C and s2=A explores whether s3 has further optimal levels or complementary trade-offs.
Label s3=D dramatically reduced both objectives on s1=C. Testing s1=E with s2=A and s3=D could yield an even lower f2, as s1=E achieved lower f2 than s1=C on s3=B.
s3=D drastically reduced both objectives. When paired with s3=B, s1=B had the lowest f1 among all sites. Testing s1=B, s2=A, s3=D may yield an even lower f1 than s1=C.
Switching to s3=D consistently reduces f2 by ~768 across all s1 choices. Testing s1=D with s2=A and s3=D could achieve a new minimum on f2.
Site s3=D yielded the best trade-offs across all s1 choices evaluated so far. Evaluating s1=A with s3=D explores whether s1=A achieves a non-dominated trade-off between f1 and f2.

With s3=D established as globally optimal across all s1, s2=B remains untested for s3=D outside s1=D/A. Testing s1=E, s2=B, s3=D checks for potential s1-s2 interactions that could improve the Pareto front.
s1=A achieved the best f2 so far. Testing s1=A with s3=A investigates whether another s3 setting can further push the low-f2 boundary of the Pareto front.
Testing s1=C s2=B s3=D to probe if s2=B provides an f2 reduction for s1=C, while exploiting the globally dominant s3=D setting.
Evaluating unexplored label s3=C with s1=A to check if it provides further trade-off improvements along the low-f2 edge of the Pareto front.
Explore whether s2=B interacts differently with s1=B on the Pareto-optimal s3=D branch, testing for trade-off improvements against s1=B, s2=A, s3=D.
With s3=D dominating, s1=B s2=A achieves the lowest f1. Testing s1=B s2=A with s3=C probes for potential fine-grained trade-offs or non-linear interactions at the minimal-f1 boundary.
Vary s1 to A while holding s2 and s3 at baseline values to test the main effect of s1.
Isolate s1 by evaluating label B with s2 and s3 at baseline, mapping the marginal impact of s1 on both objectives.
Explore remaining s1 values while keeping s2 and s3 constant to identify whether label C achieves better trade-offs than A, B, or D.
Evaluate the remaining untested label for s1 (E, which ignores s2) while holding s3=D to complete the single-variable scan of s1.
s1=E drastically lowers f1. Because s2 is ignored when s1=E, exploring the effect of s3 with s1=E helps optimize the remaining trade-offs efficiently.
s1=E drastically lowers f1. Testing s3=B with s1=E explores if s3 can improve f2 to under 3200 and dominate the remaining Pareto front.
